title: Printer not printing or shows offline
answer: An offline printer may have a connection, queue or device problem.
steps: Check power, paper and any displayed error code.
Check USB or network connections. For Wi-Fi, confirm the printer and computer are on the same network.
Open Windows Settings, then Bluetooth & devices, then Printers & scanners. Select the printer and check its queue.
Restart the printer and run the Windows printer troubleshooter. Ask the administrator before changing a shared printer.

title: Wi-Fi keeps dropping
answer: Dropped connections can come from coverage, interference, the device or the internet service.
steps: Compare another device in the same room.
Move closer to the access point and compare the connection.
Check that Wi-Fi is enabled and airplane mode is off.
Restart the affected computer. Ask the network administrator before restarting shared network equipment or changing its settings.

title: No internet at all
answer: Check whether the fault affects one device or the whole network.
steps: Try another device and another website.
Check Wi-Fi and network cables.
Note the router lights and compare them with its manual.
For a home connection, restart the router if you can safely interrupt service. For a workplace, contact the administrator first.
Contact the provider if multiple devices remain offline.

title: Computer very slow
answer: Slow performance can have several causes; resource use helps narrow them down.
steps: Save your work and restart the computer.
Check Task Manager for high CPU, memory or disk use. High use alone does not prove a hardware fault.
Check available storage without deleting unfamiliar files.
Review startup apps with your administrator before disabling business software.

title: Computer will not turn on
answer: Check for signs of power without opening the equipment.
steps: Check the power cable and a known working socket.
Note any lights, fan sound or screen message.
Use only the correct manufacturer-approved charger.
If there is heat, swelling, smoke, liquid damage or a burning smell, stop using it and contact a technician.

title: Pop-ups, virus or ransomware
answer: If ransomware or compromise is suspected, limit spread and contact your IT team.
steps: Disconnect the affected device from Wi-Fi and wired networks.
Do not enter passwords or payment details into suspicious prompts.
Preserve the error message or ransom note for the response team.
Ask IT before deleting files, reinstalling software or restoring backups.

title: Deleted files or need data recovered
answer: Recovery depends on storage type, backups and subsequent writes.
steps: Check the Recycle Bin and available backup or version history.
Stop saving new data to the affected drive.
Do not install recovery software onto that drive.
For important data, contact a recovery specialist before further attempts.

title: CCTV not recording or cannot view remotely
answer: Live viewing, recording and remote access need separate checks.
steps: Check whether live images appear on the recorder monitor. This does not verify recording.
Review recording status and storage health without formatting or initializing a drive.
Check the recorded date/time and try playback.
For remote viewing, check internet access and the official app. Ask your installer before changing firewall or port settings.

title: Email not sending or receiving
answer: Email faults may involve service availability, storage, account access or the mail app.
steps: Note the exact error without sharing credentials.
Check whether webmail works in a browser.
Check mailbox storage and connection status.
Contact your mail administrator before removing accounts or changing server settings.

title: Locked out of Windows
answer: Use the official recovery process for your account type.
steps: Check Caps Lock and keyboard layout.
For a personal Microsoft account, use Microsoft’s official account recovery page.
For a work account, contact your administrator.
Do not repeatedly guess passwords or use untrusted password-bypass software.

title: Laptop hot, loud fan, or switching itself off
answer: Heat and fan noise can have several causes and need model-specific checks.
steps: Place the computer on a hard surface with clear vents.
Save your work and stop using equipment that is unusually hot or shuts down repeatedly.
If there is smoke, swelling or a burning smell, disconnect power if safe and seek professional help.
Do not open the power supply or attempt internal repairs without appropriate training.

title: Backups and protecting data
answer: Protect backups from the same failures that could affect your working data.
steps: Keep separate backup copies, including an offline or appropriately isolated copy.
Test a restore to a separate location and verify the restored files.
Review backup failures and access permissions with your administrator.
